hints: Write the general term in the binomial expansion of $\left(px^2 + \frac{4}{p}x\right)^5$ using the formula $\binom{5}{r}(px^2)^{5-r}\left(\frac{4}{p}x\right)^r$.
Determine the value of $r$ that gives the term in $x^7$: $(x^2)^{5-r}(x)^r = x^{10-r} = x^7 \implies r = 3$.
Evaluate the coefficient $\binom{5}{3}p^{5-6}(4^3) = \frac{640}{p}$, set it equal to 1280, and solve for $p$.
walkthrough:
Write the general $(r+1)$-th term in the binomial expansion of $\left(px^2 + \frac{4}{p}x\right)^5$ using the Binomial Theorem:
$$T_{r+1} = \binom{5}{r}\left(px^2\right)^{5-r}\left(\frac{4}{p}x\right)^r = \binom{5}{r}p^{5-2r}4^r x^{10-r}$$

Set the power of $x$ equal to $7$ to identify the required term:
$$10 - r = 7 \implies r = 3$$

Calculate the coefficient of $x^7$ with $r = 3$:
$$\text{Coefficient} = \binom{5}{3}p^{5-6}(4^3) = 10 \times p^{-1} \times 64 = \frac{640}{p}$$

Equate the coefficient to $1280$ and solve for $p$:
$$\frac{640}{p} = 1280 \implies p = \frac{640}{1280} = \frac{1}{2}$$
